# SPD-068 — Split main.js (6724 lines) into a main/ directory and Electron-free src/ modules

## Brief
Plan: [[docs/spikes/bad-036/main|main spike]] (Amandine, BADS-036), with the scout survey [[docs/spikes/bad-036/main-smoke|main-smoke]] as raw input only (its section A has known defects; the spike's section 2e is the corrected list).

Proposed: a new main/ directory beside main.js, with orchestrating IPC handler groups under main/ipc/ and the walkthrough as main/smoke/<leg>.js; four Electron-free modules plus one function move into src/ with unit tests. The require graph is acyclic by construction, and every main/ module obeys two rules: no work at load time, and never export a let (state is read through accessors). main.js keeps lifecycle and becomes an ordered registerIpc list. Eight files over 250 are argued, the largest about 300 (license-refresh, updates). Needs package.json build.files main/**/*, and test/collabthumb.test.js must read main/. The directory must not be named server or site (the asar leak check).

Cross-ticket: section 2e lists every renderer name the smoke walkthrough evaluates; the renderer/app.js split keeps them.

Verification: function-body diff for pure moves, npm test for the new src/ modules, scoped and full npm run smoke, and a packaged smoke once build.files changes (npm run dist, then the packaged binary with --smoke, SMOKE_DIR and BT_LIBRARY_ROOT). The updater has no local proof and moves whole and unchanged; the next release's update is its test.

**Gate.** Queued until Eric approves the proposed file layout in the spike. Phase 2 does not start before that approval, and an approval that changes the layout is written into the spike's section 4 first.

**Rules for Phase 2, from BAD-036.** Split by responsibility; 250 lines is where a file gets a second look, not a cap, and every file left over 250 is argued in the spike's section 6. Every PR is a pure move: no statement is edited, a bug found on the way is its own ticket, and the spike's behaviour-preservation check (section 8) runs on every PR. The public surface in section 2 is the compatibility contract and does not change. Extraction order follows section 9: shared constants, types and pure utilities first, then state and services, then sub-components or handlers, then the entry file reduced to an orchestrator. Verification is the implementing-changes skill's tier for the files touched, quoted in each PR.

## Size, persona and model decision
Phase 2: one engineer on opus per PR in the spike's section 9, in a worktree on a feat/bad-nnn branch after bash scripts/worktree-init.sh; a reviewer at fable tier (opus while the Fable limit holds) checks each PR's pure-move proof before it lands.
